identity.head: 510f0043917e011228f03f7b66f6d99e7acf94ca
identity.description:
Make the end-of-run review one goal check

## Summary

At the end of a goal run, crew no longer runs a skeptical code review for up to three rounds. It runs one **goal check**: a single review that asks whether the finished change does what the goal asked, with every constraint the user stated. The repo's own review (CI, a bot or a person) owns code defects, so the goal check reports one only as a suggestion. It runs once, runs no test suite, and uses a cheaper model with a shorter time limit. The review of a colleague's PR (`/crew:review`) keeps its full skeptical review on every push. Records showed that 34 of 53 runs went to the three-round cap, and only 7 of 43 blocking findings were goal misses, which is the part only crew can check.

**Ticket:** [T90 — Make the end-of-run review one goal check](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/blob/main/docs/tickets.md#t90--make-the-end-of-run-review-one-goal-check)
**Type:** Refactor

---

## Agent context

### Authority

- `docs/design.md` §15.151 (new): the decision, the user's words, the figures, and each choice below. It replaces the three-round cap of the earlier entries, which now point to it.
- `skills/project-lead/references/goal-check.md` (new) owns the goal check: the question, the one round, the labels and verdict, what follows a goal miss, and "Mark the PR ready".
- `skills/project-lead/references/skeptical-review.md` owns the round machinery both run kinds share (arming, `review_pending`, the launch order, the resume list, the ledger) and a review run's skeptical review.
- `skills/project-lead/references/review-runner.md` owns the mechanics, with one value table per run kind.

### Decisions

- **Name:** the step on a goal run is the goal check. A review run keeps the skeptical review. Record file names do not change: a goal check writes `reviews/skeptical-r<n>.md`, and `rounds[].source.kind` stays `skeptical`, so old and new records read the same. A goal check report carries `Check: goal` after `Reviewed:`.
- **Suite:** the goal check runs no suite and no gate. What is lost is a second suite run at the final head, in a separate process. Each package's criterion, the project lead's suite run at "Integrate", and CI on the PR still cover it. `reviews/baseline.md` is still written, because delivered-window ICs and CI adjudication read it.
- **Runner:** the goal check runs `claude -p --model sonnet --effort high` under `timeout 900` (15 minutes). A round at Opus took about 4 minutes, 8 at the 90th percentile, and the goal check reads less. A review run keeps `opus`, `high` and `timeout 2700`.
- **Labels:** only a goal miss can be `blocking`, in the report and in the project lead's own label. A code defect is a `suggestion` at most.
- **One round:** after the goal check, a head move on a goal run arms nothing: `crew-record.py` lists the head in `run.unreviewed_heads` with the reason `goal-check-done`, and no message names it. A goal-miss patch package gets no second check. `arm-review --past-cap` still runs one more check when the principal asks for it in words.
- **Mark the PR ready:** a `pr_url`; no `PR: draft`; `review_pending` is `null` (the goal check is adjudicated); no package `pending` or `in-flight` (a goal-miss patch has integrated); every `run.rounds` entry replied. The orchestrator's ready line and stage `pr` go at that point, not at the report.
- **Substitution:** the goal check is a goal run's replaceable step. The `Reviewers` words "goal check" and "skeptical review" both name it on a goal run. A replacement gets the goal-check instructions and runs one round, with no `codex exec resume` line. `run.steps_substituted` writes `goal-check`; `skeptical-review` stays valid in old records and on a review run.
- **Stats:** `crew-stats.py` prints a new table: goal checks run, goal checks with a goal miss, goal misses found, goal checks accepted. Older skeptical reports keep their counting.
- **`skills/review` keeps** its skeptical review whole: every head reviewed, no cap, the reviewer resume and the later-round block, the suite, Opus at high effort and the 45-minute limit. Its files changed only in pointers and names.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/project-lead/references/goal-check.md`: new; owns the goal check.
- `skeptical-review.md`: keeps the shared round machinery and the review run's stance; the three-round cap, the accepted-verdict stop and "Mark the PR ready" left it.
- `review-runner.md`: one command with a value table per run kind; a goal-check instructions block (no suite, no baseline part, no later-round part, read-only tools); "Resume the reviewer" applies to a review run only.
- `substitution.md`, `record-format.md`, `simple-path.md`, `full-path.md`, `resume.md`, `review-output.md`, `band-rubric.md`, `autonomy-contract.md`, `orchestrator-report.md`, `plan-review.md`, `SKILL.md`: point at the goal check where they named a goal run's skeptical review.
- `skills/project-lead/scripts/crew-record.py`: `GOAL_CHECK_ROUNDS = 1` in place of the cap of 3; a goal run's arming after round 1 lists the head as `goal-check-done`; `--past-cap` arms one more; a review run arms every head.
- `skills/project-lead/scripts/crew-stats.py`: the goal checks table; `goal-check` is a substitutable step.
- `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md`, `references/pr-watch.md`: a goal run's head move runs no review; a review run's rules are unchanged.
- `skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md`, `references/usage.md`: the ready line goes when "Mark the PR ready" runs; a `goal-check-done` head is not an unreviewed head for the merge.
- `skills/review/SKILL.md`, `references/later-round.md`, `references/github-review.md`: pointers and names only.
- `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`: the goal check, the model table and the layout.
- `docs/design.md`: new §15.151; earlier entries that stated the cap point to it; §15.149's "the skeptical review still read the code" gains the goal check's split of the work.
- `docs/tickets.md`: new T90.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: version 0.1.118.

### Constraints that applied

- Version rule: both manifests at 0.1.118; the orchestrator assigned 0.1.116 to the plan review and 0.1.117 to the split critic.
- One rule, one file: `goal-check.md` owns the goal run's rules, and `skeptical-review.md` keeps the shared machinery once.
- `SKILL.md` stays under 500 lines (496).
- `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md` (612 lines) and `CLAUDE.md` (314 lines) were already over their size targets before this change and grew by a few lines each for the goal-check rules and the build state. Cutting them is outside this change.

### How this was verified

- `grep -rn -i -E 'three rounds is the cap|REVIEW_ROUND_CAP *= *3' skills` prints nothing.
- `crew-record.py` against seeded temporary records: a goal run's hand-over arms round 1; after the check, `integrate --review-head B` leaves `review_pending` null and lists B as `goal-check-done`; `arm-review --head C --past-cap` arms round 2; a review run at round 3 arms round 4.
- `python3 -m py_compile` passes for both scripts. `crew-stats.py` exits 0 on the real record root and prints the goal checks table (all zero, as no run has used it); a seeded record set gave the expected counts.
- Every pointer from `skills/review` to `skeptical-review.md` and `review-runner.md` was checked against its target section.
- Every remaining `skeptical` hit in `skills`, `agents`, `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` names a review run, a kept file name or field, or history.

### Known gaps

- No real run has used the goal check: not its runner at Sonnet with the 15-minute limit, not the `Check: goal` line, not the `goal-check-done` listing in a delivered window, not the orchestrator's ready line at "Mark the PR ready", and not a substituted goal check.
- `skills/project-lead/scripts/spend.py` still labels every headless review session "skeptical review" in its output. It prices them correctly.

findings.span_text: def read_goal_checks(record: Path) -> dict: """Count the record's goal checks, as `blank_goal_checks` shapes them. A goal check is a `skeptical-r<n>.md` report with `Check: goal` in its header. Its verdict is the reply file's `Verdict after labels:` line, or the report's last `Verdict:` line when no reply file holds one. A check with the verdict `patch round needed` found a goal miss, and adds its last `Blocking count:` to `misses`. A check with `accepted` was accepted. A check with neither verdict counts as run and as nothing else: the catch rate's skip line already names it. """ counts = blank_goal_checks() directory = record / "reviews" if not directory.is_dir(): return counts for name in sorted(os.listdir(directory)): found = SKEPTICAL_REPORT.match(name) if not found: continue try: text = (directory / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") except OSError: continue if not CHECK_GOAL.search("\n".join(text.splitlines()[:HEADER_LINES])): continue counts["run"] += 1 verdicts = VERDICT.findall(text) verdict = verdicts[-1].strip().lower() if verdicts else None reply = directory / f"skeptical-r{found.group(1)}-reply.md" try: after = AFTER_LABELS.findall(reply.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")) except OSError: after = [] if after: verdict = after[-1].strip().lower() if verdict and verdict.startswith("patch round needed"): counts["missed"] += 1 blocking = BLOCKING_COUNT.findall(text) counts["misses"] += int(blocking[-1]) if blocking else 0 elif verdict and verdict.startswith("accepted"): counts["accepted"] += 1 return counts
findings.suggested_fix: Seed a record with Check: goal reports (patch round needed, accepted, and a reply file overriding the verdict) and assert the four counts.

findings.span_text: | `watch` | `{last_polled_at, seen_ids, head, draft, held, queued}`, the cursor of the PR watch. `last_polled_at` is the ISO-8601 UTC time a re-armed monitor polls from: a `review` or `comment` older than it is not reported. `seen_ids` lists every item id the project lead has reported to the principal, a check's `<link>@<startedAt>` id included and the id of a `ready`, `merged`, `queued`, `dequeued` or `closed` line excluded. `head` is a sha, the last PR head the project lead knows. It joins the first write, and a `push` wake updates it after the item is sorted. The project lead also writes it after every push it makes itself. `draft` is the last draft state the project lead itself knows. `held` lists the items, each `{kind, id, author, at, summary}`, that arrived while a round of the same kind was open, until their own round opens. `queued` is a boolean, `true` while the PR is in the merge queue as far as the project lead knows. The project lead writes it `true` on a `queued` item, and writes it back to `false` with the cursor after a `dequeued` item. `pr-watch.sh` reads it at start, and an absent key reads as `false`. Each write has one owner, which says when it runs and with which command. The first write is written by `crew:delivered-window`'s `pr-watch.md`, "The first write's cursor". The write after a wake is written by that skill's "Watch the PR", and `held` by its "Findings from a review". `draft` alone is also written by `pr-watch.md`'s "Arm the monitor" step 3, by `pr-watch.md`'s "The fallback poll" and by `skeptical-review.md`'s "Mark the PR ready". Absent on a run that never had a PR. |
